definition: .NET Full-Stack Capstone is a core concept in .NET Full Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What .NET Full-Stack Capstone is
theory.body: .NET Full-Stack Capstone describes the methods and patterns used within .NET Full Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: .NET Full-Stack Capstone is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why .NET Full-Stack Capstone matters
theory.body: Without .NET Full-Stack Capstone, systems built with .NET Full Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How .NET Full-Stack Capstone works
theory.body: The mechanism behind .NET Full-Stack Capstone follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of .NET Full-Stack Capstone.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of .NET Full-Stack Capstone
theory.body: .NET Full-Stack Capstone offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
